chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: The Club Myerdor floor show with Al Hardenbrook and Hooven
summary: Drummer Al Hardenbrook gets him a floor-show job at a mob-run club; Hooven replaces him as the better reader and drills him on parts.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah, but I went--- then I got a chance -- I knew a drummer and his name - if Ann were here she could tell me the name of that drummer - but, anyway, we went in a club right almost across from my hotel called the "Club Myerdor" and it was run by one of the mob guys and, uh, we went until like six or seven in the morning. We started at eleven at night. And, we had a floor show to play and it had dancing girls and they had adagio dancers and comedians and it was a marvelous thing. And, I got that through this drummer, Melbrook or ---

Who was from Gary, Indiana and I met him on one of the jobs with Benson guys -- he said, "Listen, I'm going to take a band in and gee, if you want the cornet part, you come on and join up." So, I did that for awhile. And, then, we got Joe Hooven in there and, of course, they needed a better reader than me to play those shows. So, of course, naturally, Hooven and I being such good friends, I talked up a storm for him and they got him in. And, uh, there was times that we used to - in my hotel room - we'd take a music stand over there
and I would learn and get my parts straight for the second parts of the floor show. So, we were practicing once in the room---
